suggested_title: Shoa Clarke - Assistant Professor of Medicine and Pediatrics at Stanford Medicine
prospect_notes: Shoa L. Clarke earned his undergraduate degree in human biology from the Division of Nutritional Sciences at Cornell University, where he also played on the club ultimate Frisbee team. He went on to earn his MD and PhD in Genetics from Stanford University School of Medicine (PhD 2013). After clinical training in internal medicine at Brigham & Women's Hospital, pediatrics at Boston Children's Hospital, and cardiovascular medicine at Stanford Hospital, he joined the Stanford faculty. He is now an Assistant Professor of Medicine (Stanford Prevention Research Center) and of Pediatrics (Cardiology) at Stanford Medicine, serving as a preventive cardiologist. His research focuses on complex disease genetics in diverse populations, integrating monogenic and polygenic risk with clinical risk, and large-scale phenotyping using EHR and medical images. He has been cited over 7,200 times and authored a New York Times op-ed titled 'How Hospitals Coddle the Rich'.

suggested_title: John Van Arnam - MD/PhD Alumnus (Stanford 2011), Pathologist in Sunnyvale CA
prospect_notes: John S. Van Arnam received his BS from Cornell University, where he was a member of the Men's Heavyweight Rowing team (1999-2000 roster). He went on to complete an MD/PhD program at Stanford University School of Medicine, graduating in the class of 2011, with research conducted in the Oro Laboratory (Department of Dermatology). After completing a residency in internal medicine at Kaiser Permanente Northern California (2011-2012) and a residency in anatomic and clinical pathology at Duke University Hospital (2012-2016), he entered practice as a pathologist in Sunnyvale, CA. He co-authored research on superficial sarcomas with CIC rearrangement published in the Journal of Cutaneous Pathology, and contributed to immunology research published in the Journal of Nuclear Medicine.
